seo-tools/backlink-checker.title: How to use a free backlink checker to check backlinks and find link opportunities
seo-tools/backlink-checker.intro: A backlink checker shows which websites link to yours, which pages they point to and what anchor text they use. Backlinks are still one of the strongest ranking signals in Google, and they increasingly shape which brands AI assistants trust and cite. This free SEO backlink checker tool analyzes a link export privately in your browser, so you can check backlinks without signing up or sharing your data.

sections.h: How to check backlinks for free
sections.p: Export your links from Google Search Console (Links, then Top linking sites or Top linked pages, then Export), or from Bing Webmaster Tools, Ahrefs Webmaster Tools or any SEO tool you already use. Paste the export into the backlink checker above with your domain, and it groups the links by referring domain, flags the anchor text mix and highlights the pages that attract the most links. Search Console is the most reliable free source because it comes straight from Google.

sections.h: What to look for in a backlink search
sections.p: Look for the number of distinct referring domains rather than total links, the share of links pointing to your money pages versus the homepage, a natural anchor text mix (mostly brand and URL anchors, few exact-match keywords), and links from sites relevant to your industry or city. A handful of relevant local or industry links is worth more than hundreds of directory links.

sections.h: How to spot toxic or spammy backlinks
sections.p: Warning signs include sudden spikes of links from unrelated foreign sites, links from obvious link farms or private blog networks, sitewide footer links with keyword anchors, and pages that exist only to link out. Google ignores most of these automatically, so disavowing is rarely needed; reserve it for a manual action or a known paid-link history.

sections.h: Turning backlink data into new links
sections.p: Use the backlink checker on two or three competitors as well as your own site. The sites linking to them but not to you are your best outreach list: industry associations, local news, suppliers, directories and publications that already link to businesses like yours. Our [link building](/link-building/) and [off-page SEO](/off-page-seo/) services do this outreach for you, and a [competitor SEO analysis](/competitor-seo-analysis/) maps the full gap.

sections.h: Choosing a structure: ccTLDs, subdomains or subfolders
sections.p: Country domains (example.de) send the strongest local signal but split authority across sites and cost more to run. Subdomains (de.example.com) are easier to host separately but are treated partly as separate sites. Subfolders (example.com/de/) keep all authority on one domain and are the right default for most US brands expanding abroad. The choice should follow your legal, hosting and team setup, not habit.

Hreflang tags tell Google which language and country each URL serves and which pages are equivalents. Every version must reference every other version and itself, use valid language and region codes, and point to indexable, canonical URLs. Missing return links and hreflang pointing to redirected or noindexed pages are the most common errors; our [technical SEO](/technical-seo/) audits check every pair.

Searchers in each market use different words, currencies, units and examples. Keyword research per country, local pricing and shipping details, and native-speaker review turn a translated page into one that ranks and converts. Machine translation without review rarely ranks.

seo-tools/serp-checker.title: SERP checker: preview your Google result and check where you rank
seo-tools/serp-checker.intro: People use "SERP checker" for two different jobs: previewing how a page will look in Google's results, and checking where a page ranks for a keyword. This free tool does the first. For positions, use our free [keyword rank checker](/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/). This guide explains both and how to use them together.

sections.p: Google cuts titles and descriptions by pixel width, not character count, and the limits differ on desktop and mobile. The preview shows where your title and description will be truncated, so you can put the keyword and the reason to click inside the visible part. A title of roughly 50 to 60 characters and a description of 120 to 160 usually fit.

sections.h: How to check where you rank
sections.p: Search the keyword in a private browser window from the location you serve, copy the result URLs and paste them into the [keyword rank checker](/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/). For accurate history across many keywords, Google Search Console's Performance report shows your average position for every query that showed your site.

sections.h: Turn the preview into more clicks
sections.p: Lead the title with the exact phrase people search, add one differentiator (a price, a timeframe, free, a location) and keep the brand at the end. In the description, answer the search in one sentence and give a reason to click. Our [meta tag checker](/seo-tools/meta-tag-checker/) confirms the tags are actually present in the page source.

sections.h: Why Google sometimes rewrites your snippet
sections.p: Google may replace a title or description it judges less relevant to the query. Matching the title to the page's main heading and the description to the page's real content reduces rewrites. If rankings rather than snippets are the problem, a [free SEO audit](/seo-audit/) shows what is holding the page back.

seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker.title: Check SEO ranking online: how to get accurate keyword positions
seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker.intro: Checking where a page ranks sounds simple, but personalization, location and device all change the results. This free keyword rank checker finds your domain's position in a results list you paste, so you see the same results your customers see. This guide covers how to get accurate positions and what to do with them.

sections.h: Get results that match your customers
sections.p: Use a private window, sign out of Google and search from the city you serve, or add the city to the keyword. Local results change street by street, which is why local businesses also use rank grids. Paste the result URLs in order and the tool shows where your domain and competitors appear.

sections.h: Search Console is the most reliable rank source
sections.p: Google Search Console reports the average position for every query that showed your site, across all locations and devices. It is the best source for trends. Use the rank checker for spot checks of specific keywords and competitors.

Positions 1 to 3 earn most clicks, positions 4 to 10 earn some, and anything past page one earns very few. Pages at positions 11 to 30 are the best opportunities: improving their title, content and internal links often moves them onto page one.

sections.h: Next steps when you rank low
sections.p: Check the page with the [SEO score checker](/seo-tools/seo-score-checker/), compare it with the pages above you, and look at links with the [backlink checker](/seo-tools/backlink-checker/). Our [SERP checker](/seo-tools/serp-checker/) helps turn the rankings you have into more clicks.

seo-tools/seo-score-checker.title: SEO score checker: what your page score means and how to raise it
seo-tools/seo-score-checker.intro: A free SEO checker gives a quick read on a page's on-page basics. This tool scores a page from 0 to 100 using 14 on-page checks and gives a fix for each issue. This guide explains what the score covers, what it cannot measure, and which fixes matter most.

sections.p: The score looks at the title, meta description, headings, word count, images and alt text, internal and external links, canonical, robots, viewport, language, Open Graph tags and structured data. These are the on-page signals you fully control.

Rankings also depend on links from other sites, competition, search intent and how well the content answers the query. A page can score 100 and still rank poorly in a competitive market, so treat the score as a checklist, not a ranking prediction.

A missing or duplicate title, a missing H1, a noindex tag, a wrong canonical and very thin content cause the biggest problems. Missing alt text, long titles and missing Open Graph tags matter less. Validate structured data with the [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).

sections.h: Check the whole site, not one page
sections.p: Site-wide problems such as blocked crawling, broken sitemaps or duplicate pages need a fuller review. Test crawl rules with the [robots.txt checker](/seo-tools/robots-txt-checker/), check the sitemap with the [sitemap checker](/seo-tools/sitemap-checker/), or request a [free SEO audit](/seo-audit/).

seo-tools/website-seo-checker.title: Website SEO checker: how to check any page's SEO basics
seo-tools/website-seo-checker.intro: This free website SEO checker reads a page's source code and reports the on-page basics: title, description, headings, images, links, canonical and structured data. Because you paste the source, it works on any page, including pages behind staging or login. This guide shows how to use it and read the results.

sections.h: How to get the page source
sections.p: Open the page in your browser, right-click and choose View page source, then copy everything and paste it into the checker. For pages built with JavaScript, compare this with what Google renders using the URL Inspection tool in Search Console.

Title and description length, the number of H1 headings, heading order, images missing alt text, internal and external links, the canonical URL, robots directives and structured data types found on the page.

Two H1 headings, a canonical pointing to another page, a leftover noindex from development, images without alt text and descriptions that are missing or duplicated across pages. Each one is quick to fix once you know it is there.

For a scored report use the [SEO score checker](/seo-tools/seo-score-checker/), for a full on-page audit use the [SEO audit tool](/seo-tools/seo-audit-tool/), and for site-wide issues book a [free SEO audit](/seo-audit/).

seo-tools/keyword-research-tool.intro: This free keyword research tool generates hundreds of keyword ideas from a seed term, grouped into questions, commercial, local and comparison searches. Ideas are only useful once they become pages, so this guide covers how to choose, group and use them.

sections.p: Use the words customers use on calls and in reviews as seeds, not industry jargon. A plumber should start with water heater repair or burst pipe, not plumbing solutions. Add your city to see local variants.

Commercial and local ideas belong on service and location pages. Question ideas belong in FAQs and guides. Comparison ideas (X vs Y) deserve their own articles. One page should target one intent, with close variants as secondary keywords.

Google Search Console shows which searches already trigger your pages. Prioritize ideas that match those queries, then check volume and difficulty in a keyword tool before writing. Our [keyword research](/keyword-research/) service does this mapping for you.

For ready-made lists for local businesses, see our guide to [SEO keywords by industry](/blog/seo-keywords-by-industry/), and check where you rank with the [keyword rank checker](/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/).

seo-tools/seo-audit-tool.title: Free SEO audit tool: run an on-page audit in minutes
seo-tools/seo-audit-tool.intro: This free SEO audit tool checks one page's HTML for titles, meta tags, headings, images, links, canonical and structured data. It is the fastest way to catch on-page mistakes before or after publishing. This guide explains how to use it and when you need a full site audit instead.

sections.p: Copy the page source (right-click, View page source) and paste it in. The audit lists every issue with a short explanation and fix. Run it on your most important pages first: home, main services and top landing pages.

On-page issues live in the page itself. Technical issues such as slow loading, blocked crawling, redirect chains and index bloat need a site-wide crawl. Check crawl rules with the [robots.txt checker](/seo-tools/robots-txt-checker/) and sitemaps with the [sitemap checker](/seo-tools/sitemap-checker/).

Noindex tags on pages you want ranked, wrong canonicals, missing titles and duplicate content come first. Then headings, descriptions, internal links and alt text. Structured data errors can be checked with the [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).

sections.h: When to get a full audit
sections.p: If traffic dropped, pages are not being indexed or you are planning a redesign, a full [SEO audit](/seo-audit/) covers technical health, content, links, local and AI search, with a prioritized plan.

seo-tools/meta-tag-checker.title: Meta tag checker: which meta tags matter for SEO
seo-tools/meta-tag-checker.intro: This free meta tag checker reads a page's source and reports the title, meta description, robots, canonical, Open Graph and Twitter tags. This guide explains which tags affect rankings, which affect clicks and sharing, and the mistakes worth fixing first.

sections.p: The title tag is a strong relevance signal. The robots meta tag controls whether a page can be indexed, and a leftover noindex can remove a page from Google entirely. The canonical tag tells Google which URL is the main version of a page.

sections.h: Tags that affect clicks and sharing
sections.p: The meta description does not affect rankings directly but often becomes the snippet in results. Open Graph and Twitter tags control how a page looks when shared on social media and in messaging apps. Preview snippets with the [SERP checker](/seo-tools/serp-checker/).
Duplicate titles across pages, missing descriptions, a canonical pointing to the home page, noindex left on after launch and Open Graph images that are too small. Each is quick to fix once found.

sections.h: Check the rest of the page
sections.p: For headings, images, links and structured data, use the [website SEO checker](/seo-tools/website-seo-checker/) or the [SEO score checker](/seo-tools/seo-score-checker/).

seo-tools/sitemap-checker.title: XML sitemap checker: how to validate your sitemap
seo-tools/sitemap-checker.intro: An XML sitemap tells search engines which URLs you want crawled and when they changed. This free sitemap checker counts URLs, finds duplicates and flags common format errors. This guide covers what a healthy sitemap looks like and how to fix problems.

sections.p: Only canonical, indexable URLs that return a 200 status. Leave out redirects, noindex pages, duplicates, parameter URLs and 404s. Large sites split sitemaps by type (pages, posts, products, locations) under a sitemap index.
The lastmod date should change only when the page content changes. Sitemaps that set every URL to today's date on every request teach search engines to ignore the field.

Add the sitemap URL to robots.txt and submit it in Google Search Console. The Sitemaps and Pages reports show how many submitted URLs are indexed and why others are excluded. Test robots rules with the [robots.txt checker](/seo-tools/robots-txt-checker/).

A clean sitemap helps discovery but does not force indexing. Thin or duplicate content and weak internal links are more common causes. Our [indexing case study](/blog/how-we-got-our-pages-indexed/) shows what moved a site from 17 to 123 indexed pages.

seo-tools/robots-txt-checker.title: Robots.txt checker: test what crawlers can access
seo-tools/robots-txt-checker.intro: A single wrong line in robots.txt can hide a whole site from Google or from AI search engines. This free robots.txt checker tests whether a URL is allowed or blocked for Googlebot, Bingbot and AI crawlers like GPTBot based on your rules. This guide covers how robots.txt works and the mistakes to avoid.

sections.p: Rules are grouped by user-agent. The most specific matching group applies, and within it the longest matching Allow or Disallow rule wins. A blank Disallow allows everything; Disallow: / blocks the whole site for that crawler.

sections.h: Robots.txt does not remove pages from Google
sections.p: Blocking a URL stops crawling, not indexing. A blocked page can still appear in results if other sites link to it. To keep a page out of Google, allow crawling and use a noindex tag, which you can confirm with the [meta tag checker](/seo-tools/meta-tag-checker/).

GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended follow robots.txt. Blocking them can keep your content out of AI answers. Businesses that want to be cited usually allow them; see [generative engine optimization](/geo/).

A staging Disallow: / left on after launch, blocking CSS and JavaScript Google needs to render pages, and forgetting the Sitemap line. Add your sitemap and check it with the [sitemap checker](/seo-tools/sitemap-checker/).

seo-tools/schema-checker.title: Schema checker: validate JSON-LD structured data
seo-tools/schema-checker.intro: Structured data helps search engines and AI systems understand what a page is about: a business, a service, a product, an article or an FAQ. This free schema checker validates JSON-LD and shows which types and required properties are present. This guide covers which schema types matter and how to avoid errors.

sections.p: Organization or LocalBusiness on the home page, BreadcrumbList on every page, Service on service pages, Article or BlogPosting on posts, Product on product pages and FAQPage where a page has unique questions and answers.

sections.h: Structured data must match the page
sections.p: Markup has to describe content visible on the page. Reviews, prices or FAQs that only exist in the markup can lead Google to ignore it or apply a manual action. Keep business name, address and phone identical to your Google Business Profile.

Valid markup makes a page eligible for rich results; Google decides whether to show them. Google has reduced FAQ rich results for most sites, but FAQ markup still helps search and answer engines parse questions; see [answer engine optimization](/aeo/).
Check markup with this tool and with Google's Rich Results Test after publishing. For the rest of the page, use the [SEO score checker](/seo-tools/seo-score-checker/).

seo-company.title: SEO company near me: how to find, compare and choose one
seo-company.intro: An SEO company improves how often your business appears in Google, Google Maps and AI answers for the searches your customers make, then turns that visibility into calls, leads and sales. This guide explains what an SEO company actually does, how it differs from an SEO agency or consultant, how to find a good one near you or remotely, and what it should cost.

sections.h: What does an SEO company do?
sections.p: A good SEO company fixes the technical health of your site, maps every important search to one page, improves or writes those pages, optimizes your [Google Business Profile](/google-business-profile-seo/), earns links and mentions from other sites, and reports results from Google Search Console. Work runs in a fixed order: audit, foundations, then content and authority.

sections.h: SEO company vs SEO agency vs SEO consultant
sections.p: "SEO company" and "SEO agency" usually mean the same thing: a team that does the work for you. An [SEO consultant](/seo-consulting/) sets the strategy and reviews your team's work while your staff implements it. Choose a company or agency when you need execution, and a consultant when you have in-house people who can ship changes.

sections.h: Finding an SEO company near you
sections.p: Searching "SEO company near me" shows agencies close to you, but location matters less than whether the team understands your market. A remote company can rank you anywhere if it checks your visibility across your real service area with a rank grid. RankEmpire works remotely with US businesses and runs local programs in cities including [New York](/locations/new-york/), [Chicago](/locations/chicago/), [Houston](/locations/houston/), [Phoenix](/locations/phoenix/), [Dallas](/locations/dallas/) and [Los Angeles](/locations/los-angeles/); see [all locations](/locations/).

sections.h: How much does an SEO company cost?
sections.p: Most small businesses pay $500 to $2,500 a month, multi-location and e-commerce programs $2,000 to $8,000, and national programs more. RankEmpire's local plans start at $599 a month, month to month after a three-month onboarding. Our guide on [how much SEO costs](/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) explains what drives the price, and our [SEO packages](/seo-packages/) list what each plan includes.

sections.h: How to choose the best SEO company
sections.p: Ask for real Search Console results shared with permission, a named strategist who does the work, a 90-day plan in order, how they earn links and who owns the work if you stop. Avoid guaranteed rankings, results promised in 30 days and long lock-in contracts. Our guide on [how to choose an SEO company](/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/) lists twelve questions, and our [verified results](/case-studies/) show the reports we share.

sections.h: How long does an SEO company take to show results?
sections.p: Expect early movement on long-tail and local searches in 60 to 90 days, meaningful gains on core terms in four to six months, and compounding growth after that. Impressions in Search Console rise first, then positions, then clicks and leads, as shown in our [indexing case study](/blog/how-we-got-our-pages-indexed/).

local-seo.title: Local SEO services: how to rank in Google Maps and the local pack
local-seo.intro: Local SEO is the work that puts a business in the Google Maps results and the local pack, the three map listings shown for searches like "plumber near me" or "dentist in Austin". This guide explains what local SEO and map SEO services include, how the local pack is ranked and what results to expect. For plans and prices, see our [local SEO packages](/seo-packages/local-seo/).

sections.h: How Google ranks the local pack
sections.p: Google ranks local results on three factors: relevance (how well your profile and site match the search), distance (how close you are to the searcher) and prominence (reviews, links, mentions and overall reputation). You cannot change distance, so local SEO works on relevance and prominence.

A complete [Google Business Profile](/google-business-profile-seo/) with the right categories, services, hours and photos; consistent business details across directories; one page per service and per real service area; a steady review flow; local links from news, associations and partners; and a rank grid to measure visibility across your area.

Most gains come from fixing the primary category, adding every service to the profile, posting weekly, earning reviews that mention the job and the area, and building pages that match each service. Our [Google Business Profile checklist](/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) lists every field to complete.

Each location needs its own verified profile, its own landing page with unique local detail and consistent details everywhere. Copying one page and swapping the city name rarely works. See how we approach cities like [Chicago](/locations/chicago/) and [Houston](/locations/houston/).

Profile fixes and reviews often move map rankings within 30 to 60 days; competitive city terms take three to six months. Our [90-day local SEO roadmap](/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/) shows the order of work, and local plans start at $599 a month.

seo-packages/local-seo.title: Local SEO packages: what each plan includes and what it costs
seo-packages/local-seo.intro: Local SEO packages bundle the monthly work a local business needs to rank in Google Maps and local search. This page compares RankEmpire's Starter, Pro and Multi-location plans and explains how to choose the right local SEO package for your business.

sections.p: Starter is $599 a month for one location and one service area, Pro is $1,199 a month for up to three locations, and Multi-location is $2,199 a month for four or more locations. Every plan is month to month after a three-month onboarding, with no hidden fees.

sections.h: What every local SEO package includes
sections.p: Onboarding and an audit, a 90-day roadmap, Google Business Profile setup and optimization, citations, a review request system, local pages, a rank grid report and a monthly report with a strategy call, led by one dedicated strategist.

sections.h: How to choose the right plan
sections.p: Choose Starter for one location in a moderately competitive market, Pro when you have up to three locations or a very competitive category, and Multi-location for four or more locations that each need their own profile and page. Our guide on [how much SEO costs](/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) explains what drives the price.

sections.h: What makes a local SEO package worth it
sections.p: Countable monthly deliverables, reporting tied to calls and bookings, ownership of everything built for you and no long lock-in. Be wary of packages that promise guaranteed rankings or hundreds of links for a low price; see [how to choose an SEO company](/blog/how-to-choose-an-seo-company/).

seo-packages/ecommerce-seo.title: Ecommerce SEO packages: what is included and how pricing works
seo-packages/ecommerce-seo.intro: Ecommerce SEO packages cover the monthly work an online store needs to rank category and product pages and turn organic traffic into revenue. This guide explains what RankEmpire's Launch, Scale and Enterprise ecommerce SEO packages include and how ecommerce SEO pricing is set.

sections.h: How ecommerce SEO pricing is set
sections.p: Pricing depends mainly on catalog size and technical complexity. Launch suits stores up to 500 products, Scale stores up to 5,000 products, and Enterprise larger catalogs that need a template-level technical program. Each plan is quoted after a free audit so the scope matches the store.

Technical fixes for faceted navigation and duplicate pages, category and product page optimization, product schema, buying guides that answer pre-purchase questions, internal linking between categories and products, and a monthly revenue report. See our [ecommerce SEO](/ecommerce-seo/) service for the full approach.

Category pages usually target the highest-volume commercial searches, so most programs start there: unique introductions, clear filters, internal links and FAQs. Product pages follow with unique descriptions, specifications and reviews.

Match the plan to your catalog and goals, ask for countable monthly deliverables and reporting tied to organic revenue, and make sure you own all content created. Compare all plans on our [SEO packages](/seo-packages/) page.

enterprise-seo.title: Enterprise SEO services: how large websites grow organic search
enterprise-seo.intro: Enterprise SEO covers sites with thousands of pages, several teams and complex technology. The work is less about single keywords and more about templates, crawl efficiency, governance and scale. This guide explains what enterprise SEO services and packages include.

sections.p: Large sites are fixed at the template level: one change to a category, product or location template can improve thousands of pages. We prioritize crawl efficiency, indexation control, internal linking, page speed and structured data across templates; see [technical SEO](/technical-seo/).

sections.h: Content at scale without thin pages
sections.p: Programmatic pages only work when each page carries unique, useful data. We help define which page types deserve to exist, set content standards and retire or merge pages that compete with each other.

Enterprise SEO depends on engineering, product, content and legal teams. We set SEO requirements for releases, review changes before launch and monitor for regressions, which protects rankings during redesigns and migrations.

Enterprise programs are scoped after an audit of the site, teams and goals, and usually combine technical SEO, content strategy, [international SEO](/international-seo/) where needed, and authority building. Compare options on our [SEO packages](/seo-packages/) page or book a [free strategy call](/book-a-call/).

technical-seo.title: Technical SEO services: what a technical SEO audit fixes
technical-seo.intro: Technical SEO makes sure search engines can crawl, render, understand and index your site, and that pages load fast on mobile. If the technical foundation is broken, content and links cannot do their job. This guide explains what technical SEO services cover and what to fix first.

sections.p: Robots.txt rules, XML sitemaps, canonical tags, noindex tags, redirects and internal links decide which pages search engines find and index. Test crawl rules with our [robots.txt checker](/seo-tools/robots-txt-checker/) and sitemaps with the [sitemap checker](/seo-tools/sitemap-checker/).

Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift measure loading, responsiveness and visual stability. Typical fixes: compressed and correctly sized images, less render-blocking CSS and JavaScript, and reserved space for images and embeds.
Schema markup describes your business, services, articles, products and FAQs in a format search and answer engines understand. Validate it with our [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).
Parameter URLs, near-duplicate pages and thin pages waste crawl budget and can hold rankings back. A technical audit finds them and decides whether to merge, improve, canonicalize or remove each one.

Every program starts with a [technical SEO audit](/seo-audit/) that ranks issues by impact. Our [indexing case study](/blog/how-we-got-our-pages-indexed/) shows what fixing these issues did for our own site, and [technical SEO basics](/blog/technical-seo-basics/) covers the essentials.

link-building.title: Link building services: how to earn backlinks that move rankings
link-building.intro: Links from other websites remain one of the strongest signals Google uses to judge authority. White hat link building earns those links with content, relationships and digital PR instead of buying them. This guide explains what link building services include and how to judge the quality of a backlink.

sections.p: A good backlink comes from a real site relevant to your industry or location, sits inside content people read, and is earned rather than paid for. One link from a local newspaper or industry association is worth more than hundreds from unrelated directories. Check a link profile with our [backlink checker](/seo-tools/backlink-checker/).

Original data and guides worth citing, digital PR and expert commentary, local sponsorships and partnerships, supplier and association listings, unlinked brand mentions turned into links, and guest contributions on relevant sites.

Local businesses benefit most from chamber of commerce listings, local news coverage, community sponsorships, supplier dealer locators and partner businesses. These also strengthen [local SEO](/local-seo/) and map rankings.

Private blog networks, paid link packages, link exchanges at scale and spammy directories can lead to penalties. Read why these tactics fail in [why most SEO campaigns fail](/blog/why-most-seo-campaigns-fail/).

Track referring domains, the relevance of linking sites, brand mentions and, most importantly, ranking and traffic changes for the pages you are building authority for. See also [off-page SEO](/off-page-seo/).

geo.title: Generative engine optimization: how to get cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews
geo.intro: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the work of making a brand easy for AI systems to find, understand, trust and cite when they write answers. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews read several sources and combine them; GEO makes sure your business is one of those sources. No one can guarantee a citation, but these practices make one far more likely.

sections.p: Most AI answers start from a search index, then pick passages that answer the question clearly, come from trusted sites and contain specific facts. Pages that already rank, use clear headings and state concrete numbers are cited far more often than vague pages. Our guide to [AEO vs GEO vs SEO](/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo/) explains the differences.

sections.h: Make your brand a clear entity
sections.p: Use one consistent name, description, address and service list across your website, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, directories and press. Organization and Person structured data that link to those profiles help systems connect the facts. Validate markup with our [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).

Prices, timelines, processes, comparisons and original data are what AI systems quote. Replace adjectives with facts, answer one question per section and keep pages updated with visible dates. Our [indexing case study](/blog/how-we-got-our-pages-indexed/) is an example of original data.

sections.h: Earn mentions beyond your own site
sections.p: For "best" and comparison questions, AI answers lean on third-party lists, reviews and articles. Directory profiles, reviews, expert quotes in the press and inclusion in industry roundups all raise the chance of being named; see [link building](/link-building/).

sections.h: Let AI crawlers in and measure
sections.p: Allow GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended in robots.txt (check with our [robots.txt checker](/seo-tools/robots-txt-checker/)), publish an llms.txt summary, and track a fixed set of prompts monthly to see whether your brand is named. See also [answer engine optimization](/aeo/) and [AI agent optimization](/blog/ai-agent-optimization/).

content-seo.title: Content SEO: how to write pages that rank and convert
content-seo.intro: Content SEO is the planning, writing and updating of pages so they match what people search, answer it better than competing pages and lead readers to act. This guide covers how we plan and produce content that earns rankings, featured snippets and AI citations.

sections.p: Every page targets one intent: a service page for people ready to hire, a guide for people researching, a comparison for people choosing. Map each keyword to one page with [keyword research](/keyword-research/) so pages do not compete with each other.

Put a direct answer in the first sentences under each heading, then add detail, examples, prices and steps. Clear question-style headings and short paragraphs help Google and answer engines extract passages; see [answer engine optimization](/aeo/).

Named authors with real credentials, specific examples, original data and honest limits make content more trustworthy to readers and to search engines. Generic text that could describe any business rarely ranks.

Updating pages that already get impressions is usually faster than writing new ones. Use Search Console to find queries a page shows for, add sections that answer them and improve the title. Our [SEO keywords by industry](/blog/seo-keywords-by-industry/) guide shows how to group keywords into pages.

Link guides to the service pages they support and service pages to related guides, so authority flows through the site and readers find the next step. See [on-page SEO](/on-page-seo/) for the page-level checklist.

keyword-research.title: Keyword research services: how to choose keywords that bring customers
keyword-research.intro: Keyword research finds the searches your customers make and decides which page should target each one. Done well, it prevents wasted content, pages that compete with each other and rankings that never turn into leads. This guide explains our keyword research process.

sections.p: We combine your Search Console data (searches that already show your site), keyword tools for volume and difficulty, competitor rankings and the words customers use on calls and in reviews. Try our free [keyword research tool](/seo-tools/keyword-research-tool/) for quick ideas.

Service and local keywords go to service and location pages, question keywords to FAQs and guides, comparison keywords to comparison articles. One page targets one intent with close variants as secondary keywords.
High-intent keywords with moderate competition usually pay back fastest, especially long-tail and local terms. Broad, highly competitive terms are long-term targets that need authority first.

The result is a keyword map: each important keyword assigned to one page, with a primary keyword, secondary keywords and the questions to answer. See starter lists in our [SEO keywords by industry](/blog/seo-keywords-by-industry/) guide.

Rankings and impressions in Search Console show which targets are moving. Pages at positions 11 to 30 get attention first. Check positions with our [keyword rank checker](/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/).

on-page-seo.title: On-page SEO: the checklist for every page you want to rank
on-page-seo.intro: On-page SEO covers everything on the page itself that helps it rank: the title, headings, content, images, internal links and structured data. This guide is the checklist we apply to every page we optimize.

sections.p: Lead the title with the primary keyword, keep it under about 60 characters and make it worth clicking. Write a description of 120 to 160 characters that answers the search and gives a reason to click. Preview both with our [SERP checker](/seo-tools/serp-checker/).
One H1 that states the topic, H2s for the main questions, short paragraphs, lists and tables where they help. Clear structure helps readers, Google and answer engines.
Answer the search fully: what, how, how much, how long and what to do next. Add specific details only you can provide, such as prices, process and examples. See [content SEO](/content-seo/).

Descriptive alt text, compressed images with set dimensions, links to related pages and from them, and structured data for the page type. Check pages with our [SEO score checker](/seo-tools/seo-score-checker/) and [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).
A self-referencing canonical, no accidental noindex, a mobile-friendly layout and fast loading. Site-wide technical issues are covered by [technical SEO](/technical-seo/).

seo-for-tutors.title: Tutoring SEO: how tutors and tutoring centers win students from search
seo-for-tutors.intro: Parents and students search by subject, test and location: math tutor near me, SAT prep in Austin, online chemistry tutor, reading tutor for a 2nd grader. This guide explains how tutoring SEO turns those searches into booked sessions for independent tutors, tutoring centers and online tutoring companies.

sections.h: One page per subject and test
sections.p: Math, reading, writing, science, languages, SAT, ACT, AP exams and state tests each need a page that explains the approach, grade levels, session format, pricing and results. A single services page cannot rank for all of them.

Parents choose people, not brands. Profiles with qualifications, subjects, teaching experience, background checks and a short introduction help families decide and give Google clear expertise signals.

Tutoring centers need a complete [Google Business Profile](/google-business-profile-seo/) and pages for the neighborhoods and school districts they serve. Online tutors compete nationally, so subject and test pages, helpful study guides and reviews matter more than maps.
Searches rise before school starts, before midterms and finals, and in the months before SAT and ACT test dates. Publish and update test prep and back-to-school pages two to three months ahead.

Ask families to mention the subject and the improvement in reviews, and show results honestly, such as grade or score changes shared with permission. See related playbooks for [daycares and preschools](/seo-for-daycares/) and the local factors in [Boston](/locations/boston/).

google-business-profile-seo.title: Google Business Profile optimization: how to rank higher in Google Maps
google-business-profile-seo.intro: Your Google Business Profile is often the first thing a local customer sees, and for many searches it decides who gets the call. This guide explains how Google Business Profile optimization works, what to fix first and how to keep the profile ranking.

sections.p: The primary category is the strongest relevance signal on the profile. Pick the most specific category for your main revenue service, then add secondary categories only for work you actually do. A wrong primary category can keep you out of the map pack for your core searches.

Accurate name (no keyword stuffing), address or service area, hours including holidays, phone, website, services with descriptions, products, attributes and a business description. Our [Google Business Profile checklist](/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) walks through each field.
Upload real photos of your team, work and location regularly, post offers and updates weekly, and keep hours current. Active profiles give Google and customers fresh signals.
Ask every customer for a review soon after the job and ask them to mention the service and their area. Reply to every review. Reviews influence both map rankings and whether searchers choose you.

Your name, address and phone should match across your website, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp and industry directories. Inconsistent details weaken trust in the profile. See [local SEO](/local-seo/) for the full program.

ecommerce-seo.title: Ecommerce SEO: how online stores grow organic revenue
ecommerce-seo.intro: Ecommerce SEO helps online stores rank category and product pages for the searches shoppers make before they buy. Stores face problems service sites rarely do: thousands of similar pages, faceted navigation, out-of-stock products and thin descriptions. This guide covers how we approach them.

sections.h: Category pages carry the most demand
sections.p: Category searches such as "women's running shoes" usually have the most commercial volume. Give each priority category a unique introduction, helpful filters, internal links to subcategories and FAQs that answer buying questions.

Filters and sorting can create thousands of near-duplicate URLs. Decide which filtered pages deserve to be indexed, canonicalize or block the rest, and keep the sitemap limited to pages you want ranked. See [technical SEO](/technical-seo/).

sections.h: Product pages that convert and rank
sections.p: Unique descriptions, full specifications, real photos, reviews, clear shipping and return details, and Product structured data with price and availability. Validate markup with our [schema checker](/seo-tools/schema-checker/).
Keep temporarily out-of-stock pages live with a clear status and alternatives; redirect permanently discontinued products to the closest replacement or category instead of returning a 404.
Guides that answer pre-purchase questions earn links and AI citations and feed shoppers into categories. See our [ecommerce SEO packages](/seo-packages/ecommerce-seo/) for what each plan includes.

off-page-seo.title: Off-page SEO: building the authority that moves rankings
off-page-seo.intro: Off-page SEO is everything done outside your website that tells search engines and AI systems your business is trusted: links, brand mentions, reviews, directory listings and press. For new sites it is usually the biggest gap between being indexed and ranking on page one.

sections.p: Links from real sites in your industry or area remain one of the strongest ranking signals. Earn them with useful content, original data, partnerships and digital PR rather than buying them; see [link building](/link-building/).

Unlinked mentions in articles, podcasts and roundups help search engines and AI answers associate your brand with a topic. Consistent business listings (citations) on directories support local rankings.
Reviews on Google, Bing, Yelp and industry sites influence local rankings, AI recommendations and conversions. Ask consistently and reply to every review.

For agencies and service businesses, profiles on respected directories and inclusion in "best of" lists are often what AI answers quote for "best [service] in [city]" questions. See [generative engine optimization](/geo/).

Track referring domains, brand mentions, review count and rating, and ranking changes for the pages you are building authority for. Check a link profile with our [backlink checker](/seo-tools/backlink-checker/).

competitor-seo-analysis.title: Competitor SEO analysis: how to find why rivals outrank you
competitor-seo-analysis.intro: Competitor SEO analysis compares your site with the pages that rank above you to find exactly what they do better: keywords, content, links, technical health and local signals. It turns "they rank higher" into a list of specific fixes.

sections.p: Your search competitors are the sites ranking for your target keywords, which are often different from your business competitors. Directories, publishers and national agencies frequently hold the top spots alongside local rivals.

Find the keywords competitors rank for that you do not, and compare their pages with yours: depth, structure, questions answered, prices and proof. Use our [keyword research tool](/seo-tools/keyword-research-tool/) and [keyword rank checker](/seo-tools/keyword-rank-checker/) for quick checks.

Count referring domains and look at where competitors earn links and mentions: directories, press, partners, guest articles. These are often the most reusable opportunities. Check profiles with our [backlink checker](/seo-tools/backlink-checker/).
For local searches, compare Google Business Profile categories, review counts and ratings, photos and posting frequency, and how many service area pages each competitor has.

Rank gaps by impact and effort: quick wins on pages that already rank on page two, content gaps with clear demand, and longer authority work. Our [SEO consulting](/seo-consulting/) and [SEO audit](/seo-audit/) services include this analysis.

locations/manhattan.title: Manhattan SEO company: how we rank Manhattan businesses
locations/manhattan.intro: Manhattan packs more competitors per block than any other US market. This is how RankEmpire approaches local SEO in Manhattan, what a Manhattan SEO company should deliver and how to win searches when the map pack changes every few streets. For citywide work across all five boroughs, see our [New York SEO company](/locations/new-york/) page, and for Brooklyn see [Brooklyn SEO](/locations/brooklyn/).

sections.h: Start with a block-level rank grid
sections.p: Before any keyword list, we measure where you appear in the map pack across a tight grid around your address. In Manhattan the results can change within two or three blocks, so the grid shows exactly where you win, where you lose and which competitors take over.

In dense neighborhoods the [Google Business Profile](/google-business-profile-seo/) decides most local clicks. We fix categories, services and hours (including weekday and weekend differences), add real photos, post weekly and build a review flow that asks customers to mention the service and the neighborhood.

sections.h: Pages for your services and neighborhoods
sections.p: Service pages come first. Neighborhood pages follow only where you have real clients, projects or a second location, with details such as cross streets, nearby stations and local reviews. Thin pages with swapped neighborhood names are skipped.

Law firms, financial advisors and consultancies win with expertise: profiles with credentials, detailed practice area pages and mentions in industry publications. See our [law firm SEO](/seo-for-lawyers/) and [B2B SEO](/b2b-seo/) approaches.

sections.h: What results to expect in Manhattan
sections.p: Neighborhood and long-tail searches often move within 60 to 90 days; broad Manhattan terms take longer in competitive categories. Impressions rise in Search Console first, then positions, then calls and bookings. Local plans start at $599 a month.

b2b-seo.title: B2B SEO: how business-to-business companies win leads from search
b2b-seo.intro: B2B buyers research for weeks, involve several people and compare vendors carefully. B2B SEO puts your company in front of them at each stage: when they define the problem, compare solutions and shortlist vendors. This guide covers how B2B SEO differs from local or e-commerce SEO and what to build first.

sections.h: Map content to the buying journey
sections.p: Problem-aware searches need educational guides, solution searches need comparison and use-case pages, and vendor searches need product, pricing and proof pages. Map each stage to pages with [keyword research](/keyword-research/) so every important query has one owner.

B2B keywords often have small search volumes but large deal values. A term searched 50 times a month can be worth more than one searched 5,000 times if the right buyers search it. Prioritize intent and fit over volume.

Case studies, named experts, original research and clear methodology build trust with buyers and with search engines. Thought leadership earns the links and mentions B2B sites need; see [link building](/link-building/).

Most visitors are not ready to buy. Offer next steps that fit each stage: guides, calculators, templates, webinars and a clear way to [book a call](/book-a-call/). Track assisted conversions, not just last-click leads.
Larger B2B sites need clean information architecture, fast templates and controlled indexation; see [technical SEO](/technical-seo/) and [enterprise SEO](/enterprise-seo/).

saas-seo.title: SaaS SEO: how software companies grow signups from search
saas-seo.intro: SaaS SEO turns search into trials, demos and signups. Software buyers search for problems, features, integrations, alternatives and comparisons, often long before they talk to sales. This guide explains which page types drive SaaS growth and how we build them.

sections.h: Pages that match software buying intent
sections.p: Feature and use-case pages, integration pages, "alternative to" and "vs" comparison pages, pricing, templates and free tools. Each page type targets a different search intent and stage of evaluation.

Buyers search "[competitor] alternatives" and "[tool A] vs [tool B]" close to a decision. Honest, detailed comparison pages that explain trade-offs convert well and are frequently cited by AI answers.
Useful free tools attract links, rankings and product-qualified signups. RankEmpire's own [free SEO tools](/seo-tools/) are an example of this approach.

Tutorials that show the product solving a real problem rank for how-to searches and move readers toward a trial. Content should be written with input from product and customer success, not only from keyword lists.
Track signups, activated accounts and pipeline from organic search alongside rankings. See our [SaaS SEO packages](/seo-packages/saas-seo/) and [B2B SEO](/b2b-seo/) approach.
